name: Microsoft Sentinel
summary: Microsoft Sentinel is a cloud SIEM that collects logs through data connectors and runs scheduled analytics rules that raise alerts and incidents. Its pricing page describes pay-as-you-go and commitment tiers in US dollars, but the text we read shows no per-GB rates.

facts.text: Data connectors are installed from the Content hub and then configured before they start ingesting data into Microsoft Sentinel.
Scheduled analytics rules run a Kusto query on a set interval. The run interval and the lookback period can each be set from 5 minutes to 14 days.
A rule can create one incident per alert, or group up to 150 related alerts into a single incident.
Microsoft says Sentinel in the Azure portal stops being supported after March 31, 2027, and is then available only in the Defender portal.
The analytics tier can be paired with a data lake tier that keeps data for up to 12 years.
The pricing page describes commitment tiers that reserve daily ingestion from 100 GB to 50,000 GB, with savings of up to 52% against pay-as-you-go.

plans.name: Pay-as-you-go
plans.unit: per GB ingested into the analytics tier
plans.notes: No per-GB figure appears in the pricing page text we read. The page links to the Microsoft Sentinel cost estimator.

plans.name: Commitment tiers
plans.unit: per day of reserved ingestion, 100 GB to 50,000 GB
plans.notes: Savings of up to 52% against pay-as-you-go, per the page. No dollar figure appears in the text we read.

hiddenCosts: The pricing page says prices are calculated in US dollars, but it shows no amounts in the text we read.
Per-GB rates and retention charges are not stated in the text, so the figures must come from the cost estimator the page links to.
